full_text_en:
Jingwei Company v. Liang Jinfu — dispute over ship mortgage debt transfer contract

Plaintiff: Jingwei Company (Hong Kong).

Legal Representative: Wu Jingwei, Hong Kong resident.

Agents ad litem: Liang Shan and Shen Hongwei, lawyers of Guangzhou Jinglun Law Firm.

Defendant: Liang Jinfu, Hong Kong citizen.

Agents ad litem: Ye Bo, lawyer of Sanya Nantian Law Firm, Hainan Province; Wang Zhengxie, lawyer of Lingao County Law Firm, Hainan Province.

On November 6, 1996, upon application by the plaintiff Jingwei Company, the Haikou Maritime Court of the People's Republic of China lawfully detained two fishing vessels, Xingfa No. 1 and Xingfa No. 2, owned by the defendant Liang Jinfu, at Sanya Port, Hainan Province. Jingwei Company then filed an action with the Haikou Maritime Court regarding a dispute over a ship mortgage debt transfer contract.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant Liang Jinfu borrowed money from Australian Credit Finance (Hong Kong) Limited (hereinafter "the Finance Company") by mortgaging Xingfa No. 1 and Xingfa No. 2 and their onboard equipment. Liang Jinfu failed to repay the loan when due. By judgment of a Hong Kong court, the plaintiff performed the repayment obligation on behalf of the defendant and simultaneously acquired from the Finance Company the mortgage rights over these two fishing vessels and their equipment. The plaintiff requested that Liang Jinfu be ordered to repay the principal debt of HK$1,933,163.26 and interest of HK$2,217,475.48, as well as compensate the plaintiff for losses of HK$255,198.60 incurred in recovering the said debt.

Defendant's Defense: The defendant had borrowed HK$3.1 million from the Finance Company, had partially repaid principal and interest, and still owed HK$1,406,327. A judgment was rendered by a Hong Kong court on this matter. Due to poor management, the defendant was unable to repay the said debt or enforce the Hong Kong court's judgment. However, the defendant owed no debt to the plaintiff. The plaintiff's claim that it had performed the repayment obligation on behalf of the defendant and that the Finance Company had transferred the ship mortgage rights and debt to the plaintiff lacked sufficient evidence. The court should dismiss the plaintiff's claim.

Facts Found by the Haikou Maritime Court: On April 23, 1988, and January 23, 1989, the defendant Liang Jinfu borrowed HK$1.1 million and HK$1.7 million respectively from the Finance Company for the purchase of Xingfa No. 1 and Xingfa No. 2, and mortgaged these two fishing vessels as security. For the first loan of HK$1.1 million secured by Xingfa No. 1, the annual interest rate was 11%, monthly repayment was HK$28,417, and it was agreed to be repaid in 60 monthly installments commencing from May 23, 1988. For the second loan of HK$1.7 million secured by Xingfa No. 2, the annual interest rate was 12%, monthly repayment was HK$45,333, also agreed to be repaid in 60 monthly installments commencing from February 23, 1989. In addition, on January 24, 1990, Liang Jinfu entered into an agreement with the Finance Company to purchase fishing equipment valued at HK$407,988 by way of a lease. It was agreed that Liang Jinfu would pay the Finance Company a monthly rent of HK$11,333 on the 24th of each month for 36 months commencing from February 24, 1990, and then pay a final HK$20 to obtain ownership of the fishing equipment. The mortgages created by Liang Jinfu over Xingfa No. 1 and Xingfa No. 2 were registered with the Hong Kong Marine Department, with the Finance Company as mortgagee.

Subsequently, because the defendant Liang Jinfu failed to repay the loans in accordance with the agreements, upon application by the Finance Company, the Supreme Court of Hong Kong rendered judgments on September 29, 1993, and October 13, 1993, ordering Liang Jinfu and his loan guarantor Liang Shuji to pay the Finance Company a total of HK$1,933,163.26 plus interest. Liang Jinfu raised no objection to this.

Because the defendant Liang Jinfu did not comply with the Hong Kong court judgments and went fishing outside Hong Kong without returning, the Finance Company was unable to realize its claim. On November 21, 1995, the Finance Company entered into a mortgage debt sale agreement and an implementing mortgage debt assignment deed with the plaintiff Jingwei Company. The agreement stipulated that the Finance Company would assign to Jingwei Company all outstanding mortgage debts listed in Appendix 1 of the agreement totaling HK$9,011,666, including Liang Jinfu's debt of HK$1,292,997 secured by Xingfa No. 1 and Xingfa No. 2, and a debt of HK$113,330 for the hire-purchase of a set of fishing equipment, totaling HK$1,406,327. Jingwei Company paid HK$2.8 million to the Finance Company for this assignment of rights. On December 18, 1996, Jingwei Company had completed the payment of the said amount. The Finance Company also served the debt assignment documents to Liang Jinfu's residence in Hong Kong and notified the Hong Kong Marine Department.

Opinion of the Haikou Maritime Court:

This is a dispute over a contract for the assignment of a ship mortgage debt involving Hong Kong. Pursuant to Article 243 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court has jurisdiction over the case. Although the mortgage loan contract between the defendant Liang Jinfu and the Finance Company, and the debt assignment contract between the Finance Company and the plaintiff Jingwei Company, both stipulated that Hong Kong law would apply to the resolution of contractual disputes, neither Jingwei Company nor Liang Jinfu has raised a request for the application of law, nor have they provided the relevant Hong Kong law. Therefore, it shall be deemed that the parties have not chosen the law to be applied to the dispute. Pursuant to Article 145(2) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "If the parties to a foreign-related contract have not made a choice, the law of the country with which the contract is most closely connected shall be applied," the civil law of the People's Republic of China, being the law of the place where the subject matter of the contract is located, shall be applied to this case.

The plaintiff Jingwei Company and the defendant Liang Jinfu do not raise any objection to the mortgage loan contract and the hire-purchase mortgage contract entered into between Liang Jinfu and the Finance Company, and the contents of these contracts do not violate the social public interests of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, these contracts are lawful and valid. Under the contracts, Liang Jinfu failed to repay the debt, and the Finance Company resorted to legal proceedings, which resulted in judgments by the Supreme Court of Hong Kong. Liang Jinfu also does not object to these judgments, so the judgments constitute a legal fact in this case. As the creditor confirmed by the contracts and the judgments, the Finance Company, by way of a contract, assigned its claim for value to Jingwei Company for enforcement, and simultaneously served the debt assignment documents to Liang Jinfu's residence in Hong Kong and notified the Hong Kong Marine Department. For an assignment of a debt, the original creditor need only inform the debtor of the assignment so that the debtor knows to whom performance is due; the consent of the debtor is not required. As long as the assignment is notified, it is valid. Liang Jinfu had been away from his Hong Kong residence for a long period. The Finance Company served the debt assignment documents to that residence. This method of service complies with legal provisions. Whether Liang Jinfu actually received the debt assignment documents does not affect the validity of the assignment agreement. This assignment agreement is binding not only on the Finance Company and Jingwei Company, but also on Liang Jinfu. In fact, Jingwei Company has performed the obligations stipulated in the debt assignment agreement and has become the new creditor of Liang Jinfu. Article 106(1) of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "Citizens and legal persons who breach a contract or fail to perform other obligations shall bear civil liability." Article 111 provides: "If a party fails to perform its contractual obligations, or performs them in a manner inconsistent with the agreed terms, the other party is entitled to demand performance or take remedial measures, and is entitled to claim damages." The claim asserted by Jingwei Company against Liang Jinfu shall be upheld. The defense of Liang Jinfu that he owes no debt to Jingwei Company and that the assignment agreement is invalid cannot be sustained. As for the amount of the assigned debt, the assignment agreement states HK$1,406,327, while the Hong Kong court judgment confirms HK$1,933,163.26. The judgment amount is greater than the assignment amount, and they differ. Although the total debt assigned by the Finance Company to Jingwei Company is larger than the debt under the name of the debtor Liang Jinfu, since the assignment agreement has specified the specific debt amount under the name of each debtor, the claim of Jingwei Company based on the amount in the Hong Kong court judgment cannot be upheld. The amount specified in the debt assignment agreement shall prevail. As for the interest claim of Jingwei Company, it shall also be calculated based on the interest rate stipulated in the mortgage loan contract between the original creditor and Liang Jinfu. Jingwei Company's claim for compensation of debt recovery costs is not supported due to insufficient evidence.

In summary, the Haikou Maritime Court rendered the following judgment on January 18, 1997:

1. The defendant Liang Jinfu shall repay the plaintiff Jingwei Company HK$1,406,327, plus interest of HK$200,167.21 (calculated at the annual interest rate of 12% as per the mortgage contract, from November 21, 1995, to January 28, 1997), totaling HK$1,606,494.21. This amount shall be paid within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect; any delay shall result in double the interest as penalty.
2. The other claims of the plaintiff Jingwei Company are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee: HK$32,039, to be borne by the plaintiff in the amount of HK$20,357 and by the defendant in the amount of HK$11,682.

After the first instance judgment, the defendant Liang Jinfu appealed on the grounds that "the facts concerning the debt assignment were unclear and the evidence insufficient; the original creditor did not notify the appellant, nor did it obtain the appellant's consent, which violates Article 91 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, and thus the assignment is invalid." He requested that the first instance judgment be set aside and the appellee's claim be dismissed.

After hearing, the Hainan High People's Court held that the two agreements involved in the debt assignment in this case were both signed by two directors of the Finance Company on behalf of the company, and the appellee Jingwei Company discharged the debt in accordance therewith. The Finance Company subsequently notified in writing the Hong Kong Marine Department and the appellant Liang Jinfu's residence in Hong Kong of the debt assignment. These facts have been notarially certified by notaries public commissioned by China. The facts are clear, the evidence is sufficient, and the authenticity of the debt assignment cannot be denied. Article 91 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides: "If a party to a contract assigns all or part of its contractual rights or obligations to a third party, it shall obtain the consent of the other party to the contract." The "assignment" referred to here includes both contractual rights and contractual obligations. In practice, the assignment of contractual obligations without the consent of the obligee often impairs the interests of the obligee. For this reason, the law provides such a requirement. If the assignment of a debt alone is considered, it makes no material difference to the debtor which creditor the performance is rendered to, and it does not affect the interests of either the creditor or the debtor. If the debtor incurs additional expenses due to such performance, those expenses shall be borne by the original creditor or the new creditor. Therefore, such an assignment only requires the original creditor to notify the debtor; it does not require the debtor's consent, and this is not contrary to the legislative intent. The assignment of debts, including Liang Jinfu's debt, between the Finance Company and Jingwei Company neither violates social public interests nor impairs Liang Jinfu's interests, and is lawful and valid. The grounds of appeal of Liang Jinfu cannot be sustained and shall be dismissed. The original judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and shall be affirmed. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 153(1)(i) of the Civil Procedure Law, the Hainan High People's Court rendered judgment on June 24, 1997:

Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed.
